speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing fever and abdominal tenderness after giving birth; when did your delivery occur and what was the mode of delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the prolonged labor, decreased bowel sounds, and uterine tenderness, have you noticed any changes in your vaginal discharge or foul odor, and is the pain localized specifically to the suprapubic area? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, Urinalysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The laboratory results you just received were normal, which is a good start. However, since you mentioned decreased bowel sounds and uterine tenderness, have you had any difficulty passing gas or stool? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CBC, CRP, and urinalysis results make endometritis and urinary tract infection less likely, so regarding your decreased bowel sounds and lack of gas or stool passage, have you experienced any nausea or vomiting, and did your abdomen become distended? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal CT.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound and CT results help rule out significant intra-abdominal pathology like an abscess or severe obstruction, though your decreased bowel sounds are concerning. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or shortness of breath, and are the bowel sounds completely absent or just diminished? REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer, Lactate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal D-Dimer and lactate results; this effectively rules out pulmonary embolism and sepsis-induced lactate elevation. Given your history of prolonged labor, uterine tenderness, and decreased bowel sounds without infection or obstruction, could you describe the consistency of the uterine fundus and whether you have any history of a Cesarean section or perineal lacerations?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.
